grammars.text:
# PCRE-ish regex grammar. Superset of ERE with extra group/assertion
# forms. Unsupported PCRE features (recursive patterns `(?R)`,
# conditionals `(?(...)...)`, atomic groups `(?>...)`, possessive
# quantifiers, `\K`) are REJECTED by the visitor at AST-build time
# rather than by the grammar — the grammar accepts them syntactically
# so the visitor can produce a clear error message.

pcre = pcreAlternation

pcreAlternation = pcreSequence + (pcreAltTail)*
pcreAltTail     = pcreAltSep + pcreSequence
pcreAltSep      = "|"

pcreSequence = (pcreAtomQ)*

pcreAtomQ = pcreAtom + pcreQuantSuffix?

# Order matters — the more-specific group forms must precede the
# plain capturing group so `(?:...)` etc. aren't swallowed by it.
pcreAtom = pcreNonCapturingGroup
         | pcreNamedGroupJs
         | pcreNamedGroupPython
         | pcreLookahead
         | pcreNegativeLookahead
         | pcreLookbehind
         | pcreNegativeLookbehind
         | pcreUnsupportedSpecialGroup
         | pcreGroup
         | pcreCharClass
         | pcreAnchorStart
         | pcreAnchorEnd
         | pcreDot
         | pcreEscapedAtom
         | pcreLiteralChar

# Plain group `(...)`.
pcreGroup      = pcreGroupOpen + pcreAlternation + pcreGroupClose
pcreGroupOpen  = "("
pcreGroupClose = ")"

# `(?:...)` non-capturing.
pcreNonCapturingGroup = pcreNonCapOpen + pcreAlternation + pcreGroupClose
pcreNonCapOpen        = "(?:"

# `(?<name>...)` JS-style named group.
pcreNamedGroupJs    = pcreNamedJsOpen + pcreGroupName + ">" + pcreAlternation + pcreGroupClose
pcreNamedJsOpen     = "(?<"
pcreGroupName       = /[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*/

# `(?P<name>...)` Python-style named group — normalised by the visitor.
pcreNamedGroupPython = pcreNamedPyOpen + pcreGroupName + ">" + pcreAlternation + pcreGroupClose
pcreNamedPyOpen      = "(?P<"

# Lookaround: `(?=...)`, `(?!...)`, `(?<=...)`, `(?<!...)`.
pcreLookahead         = "(?="  + pcreAlternation + pcreGroupClose
pcreNegativeLookahead = "(?!"  + pcreAlternation + pcreGroupClose
pcreLookbehind        = "(?<=" + pcreAlternation + pcreGroupClose
pcreNegativeLookbehind = "(?<!" + pcreAlternation + pcreGroupClose

# Catch-all for unsupported `(?X...)` forms — listed so the grammar
# matches them but the visitor rejects with a clear message. Avoids
# falling through to `(` as a literal (which would be confusing) or
# to a parse error (less helpful than naming the feature). Matches
# from `(?X` through the next `)`. Body is any non-`)` chars so we
# don't try to balance nested parens (the unsupported forms don't
# nest in their common usage anyway).
pcreUnsupportedSpecialGroup = /\(\?[^:<=!P][^)]*\)/

pcreCharClass = /\[\^?\]?(?:\[:[a-z]+:\]|\\.|[^\]])*\]/

pcreAnchorStart = "^"
pcreAnchorEnd   = "$"
pcreDot         = "."

pcreEscapedAtom = pcreUnsupportedEscape
                | pcreBackref
                | pcreWordBoundaryAlias
                | pcreWordBoundary
                | pcreNonWordBoundary
                | pcreClassDigit
                | pcreClassWord
                | pcreClassSpace
                | pcreClassNotDigit
                | pcreClassNotWord
                | pcreClassNotSpace
                | pcreControlEscape
                | pcreHexEscape
                | pcreUnicodeEscape
                | pcreLiteralEscape

# `\K` and `\Q` are unsupported — match them so we can throw with a
# named error rather than swallow as `pcreLiteralEscape`.
pcreUnsupportedEscape = /\\[KQ]/

# Multi-digit backrefs (PCRE allows \10, \11, etc.).
pcreBackref           = /\\[1-9][0-9]?/
pcreWordBoundaryAlias = /\\[<>]/
pcreWordBoundary      = /\\b/
pcreNonWordBoundary   = /\\B/
pcreClassDigit        = /\\d/
pcreClassNotDigit     = /\\D/
pcreClassWord         = /\\w/
pcreClassNotWord      = /\\W/
pcreClassSpace        = /\\s/
pcreClassNotSpace     = /\\S/
pcreControlEscape     = /\\[ntrfv0]/
pcreHexEscape         = /\\x[0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]/
pcreUnicodeEscape     = /\\u[0-9a-fA-F]{4}/
pcreLiteralEscape     = /\\[^bBdDwWsSntrfv0xuKQ1-9]/

pcreLiteralChar = /[^.\\\[\^$()|+*?{}]/

pcreQuantSuffix = pcreBraceQuant
                | pcreStarQ
                | pcrePlusQ
                | pcreQuestionQ

# Possessive `*+`, `++`, `?+` are caught here so the visitor can
# reject them by name. JS RegExp can't express possessive
# quantifiers.
pcreStarQ     = /\*[?+]?/
pcrePlusQ     = /\+[?+]?/
pcreQuestionQ = /\?[?+]?/
pcreBraceQuant = /\{[0-9]+(?:,[0-9]*)?\}[?+]?/
